                           SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                              PUC DOCKET NO. 59475


   JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA
    TRANSMISSION SERVICE CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF
    CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG
HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,
 CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN
          SABA, SCHLEICTER, TOM GREEN AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES

                                            §§§

                BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS



CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT OF POSITION AND POST-HEARING BRIEF OF CRAIGAN R.
          JOHNSON ON BEHALF OF THE JOHNSON BETTY ANN ESTATE


  I.      INTRODUCTION AND STATEMENT OF POSITION

  I, Craigan R. Johnson, pro se intervenor on behalf of the Johnson Betty Ann Estate, the
  owner of approximately 650 acres of active farm and ranchland directly affected by the
  U9 segment of the Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line.

  I respect that the Commission’s statutory role is to select a route, not to redesign Texas’s
  energy policy. However, PURA requires that the Commission determine whether the
  record supports the statutory requirements of least-impacting routing, community
  values, environmental integrity, and landowner protection.

  My exhibits, included in my original testimony filed in PUC Docket No. 59475 No. 3914,
  provide photographs, maps, and narrative evidence describing the severe and
  disproportionate impacts the proposed U9 route would impose upon my property and
  agricultural operations.

  For these reasons, I respectfully request that the Commission reject the U9 segment and
  select a less-intrusive route.

  II.     SUBSTANTIAL EVIDENCE STANDARD

  Texas courts require agency decisions to be supported by “such relevant evidence as a
  reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion.”
       However, conclusory statements are not substantial evidence. Expert opinions
      unsupported by underlying data cannot support an agency decision. Agencies must
      consider all relevant factors and cannot rely on incomplete analysis.

      The Commission must apply these principles here.

      III.       ROUTING IMPACTS ON THE JOHNSON BETTY ANN ESTATE

      The Johnson Betty Ann Estate is a active agricultural operation spanning approximately
      650 acres over multiple parcels. It’s value derives from its cohesive landscape,
      unbroken viewshed, wildlife habitat, grazing lands, and vineyard operations.

      The proposed alternate route link U9 bisects the largest single pasture in the Estate, and
      will be placed in such a way that:

             •   Interrupts access to an existing freshwater well
             •   Will occupy approximately 13 acres of grazing pastureland and dedicated
                 vineyard expansion grounds
             •   Impact existing hunting lease grounds
             •   Presents an ongoing risk to existing vineyard operations due to the potential of
                 herbicide drift from transmission line corridor vegetation management
                 procedures
             •   Fragments pasture and wildlife movement patterns
             •   Permanently destroys the scenic and aesthetic value of the property
             •   More than 50% of alternate route link U9 is projected over ranged pastureland,
                 while the area affected on my property is 100% ranged pastureland
             •   Creates-long-term ecological disturbances across multiple parcels

The exhibits in my original testimony from PUC Docket 59475 No. 3914 include
photographs of the property, maps showing the operations of the Estate and the alignment
of the proposed alternate route link, and documentation of the bulleted points above.

Routing a new 765-kV corridor through such land, especially through an actively operating
agricultural enterprise, is inconsistent with PURA § 37.056(c)(4)’s requirement to minimize
landowner impacts.

IV.              COMMUNITY VALUES

PURA requires the Commission to consider community values, including:

      •      Preservation of rural landscapes
      •      Protection of undisturbed ranchlands
      •      Avoidance of disproportionate burdens on individual landowners
      •      Respect for long-established land stewardship
 The proposed alternate route link U9 violates these values by placing a 765-kV through the
property, effectively bisecting the largest operating pasture. This alignment separates an
active deep-water well from existing agricultural operations, impacts an existing hunting
lease, and undermines the rural character of the property.

The exhibits in my original testimony from PUC Docket 59475 No. 3914 included
documentations of community values, rural character, and long-standing land stewardship
in the surrounding area.

   V.       ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY

The proposed alternate route link U9 would:

   •     Bisect the largest operational pasture,
   •     Fragment wildlife corridors and habitat continuity,
   •     Introduce industrial infrastructure to a previously undisturbed landscape,
   •     Require constant herbicidal vegetation management,
   •     Introduce industrial infrastructure into a previously undisturbed landscape,
   •     Create long-term ecological disturbances across multiple parcels.

My original testimony from PUC Docket 59475 No. 3914 includes documentation of
vineyard operations, existing ranch features, environmental stewardship practices, and the
location of the aforementioned water well. These in conjunction demonstrate the ecological
sensitivity of the ranch.

PURA § 37.056(c)(5) requires the Commission to protect environmental integrity. The U9
alternate route link fails this requirement by imposing unnecessary environmental harm on
intact ranchland when less-intrusive alternatives exist.

   VI.      FAILURE TO CONSIDER ALTERNATIVES

During the hearing on the merits, several intervenors questioned why the Applicant did not
evaluate generation-based alternatives, hybrid solutions, or upgrades to existing 345-kV
corridors before proposing a new 765-kV greenfield route. In response to these questions,
Mr. Rasmusson, Counsel for Oncor stated on the record that Oncor is “in the transmission
business, not the oil and gas business.”

This statement is significant. It suggests that Oncor did not evaluate alternatives not
because they were not feasible, but because they fell outside of Oncor’s preferred business
model. PURA does not allow a utility to avoid evaluating reasonable alternatives simply
because they are not part of its corporate focus.

PURA requires that an Applicant demonstrate the proposed project is the least-cost, least-
impact solution. A utility cannot satisfy this burden by declining to evaluate alternatives
because they fall outside its business model.
 Routing a 765-kV line through an existing agriculturally operating ranch – without
evaluating alternatives – is inconsistent with PURA and Texas case law requiring agencies to
consider all relevant factors.

   VII.    CONCLUSION AND REQUESTED BRIEF

For the reasons stated above, I, Craigan R. Johnson, pro se intervenor on behalf of the
Johnson Betty Ann Estate, respectfully request that the Commission:

               1. Reject the U9 segment due to its disproportionate impact on
                  undisturbed ranchlands, failure to satisfy PURA’s least-impact
                  requirement, and lack of substantial evidence supporting its necessity.
               2. Select a less-intrusive alternative that avoids intact ranchlands and
                  minimizes landowner impacts.
               3. Decline to rely on conclusory expert testimony unsupported by peer-
                  reviewed research or independent analysis.
               4. Require a complete evaluation of reasonable alternatives before
                  approving a project of this magnitude.



Respectfully submitted,

Craigan R. Johnson



7845 FM 2732
San Saba, TX 76877

(512) 968 8640

Craigan.johnson@gmail.com
